# Nvidia falls to 34% of China's AI chip market as Huawei takes 28%

An IDC shipment ledger seen by Reuters puts Nvidia at 34% of China's data-center AI chips in the first half of 2026, on shipments 44% below a year earlier. Non-GPU accelerators outsold GPUs for the first time, and Huawei took 28% of a market that kept growing.

The shipment ledger IDC, the market-research firm, compiled for China's data-center AI chips in the first half of 2026, seen by Reuters and published on October 13 ↗ , settles the argument over America's export controls 1 . Nvidia 's ▼ −0.70% — Nvidia, down 0.70 percent today share fell to 34%, on 678,000 accelerators shipped, 44% fewer than a year earlier 1 2 . Jensen Huang , Nvidia 's chief executive, has argued repeatedly that Washington's rules force his company to cede China's $50 billion AI chip market to Huawei 2 . The ledger shows the ceding is well advanced.

## The growth moved onto silicon Nvidia cannot ship

Total accelerator shipments in China reached 2.008 million units in the first half, so the market itself kept growing 1 . GPUs, the chips most widely used to train AI models and the category Nvidia dominates, fell 26% to 991,000 units, squeezed by export rules and by Beijing's requirement that companies obtain approval to import even compliant Nvidia chips 1 2 .

Every other kind of accelerator, silicon often tuned to running already-trained models, rose almost 80% to 1.016 million units and passed GPUs by volume for the first time in IDC's reported period 1 2 7 . Huawei , the Chinese equipment maker, shipped 572,000 units against just over 300,000 a year earlier, taking 28% of the whole market 1 . ## Huawei's answer is to wire weaker chips into one machine

IDC says competition in China is shifting from the performance of a single chip to how well chips work inside large computing clusters 1 . That is Huawei 's play exactly. Its Peerium architecture uses UnifiedBus links to make individually weaker domestic chips behave as one machine, and its Atlas 950 SuperCluster is built to connect up to 256,000 accelerator cards 4 . The next Ascend chip, the 960DT, has been pulled forward to the first quarter of 2027 from a planned third-quarter debut ↗ 4 5 .

The binding constraint on China's build has therefore moved from American supply to Huawei itself. TechRepublic, citing Reuters, reports the company cannot produce enough AI computing equipment to meet Chinese demand ↗ 5 . Its Ascend software ecosystem counts about 5,270 monthly active developers 6 , against the years of tooling Nvidia's CUDA platform has accumulated 5 .

## Nvidia's China demand has learned to buy elsewhere

Nvidia has already booked this door closing once, with a $4.5 billion charge on China-bound H20 inventory ↗ , the chip it designed for China, after Washington imposed license requirements in April 2025 3 . The customers it lost in the first half bought domestic silicon instead, under a Beijing approval regime that still gates Nvidia imports 1 . Winning them back would take more than a policy reversal.

Two numbers frame what to watch next. IDC expects China's total accelerator shipments to grow 19% this year even as GPU shipments fall 9% 1 7 . And the Ascend 960DT's arrival in the first quarter of 2027, pulled forward from the third, is the next data point on whether Huawei can supply the growth it is being handed 4 5 .

# Scale AI cut 89 tasks from its coding benchmark after an audit found gaming, then graded its own fix

Scale AI cut 89 tasks from the public SWE-Bench Pro leaderboard and locked its evaluation runtime after an independent preprint found the benchmark gameable. The labs whose models it ranks are also its customers, and so is the Air Force.

## Eighty-nine tasks vanish from the public ruler

The public benchmark that grades every major coding agent just got shorter. Scale AI's PVT $29B — Scale AI's, private, latest valuation $29B SWE-Bench Pro V2 ↗ cuts the public set from 731 to 642 tasks across 11 repositories, drops 89 tasks the company judged invalid, and adds a 51-task HARD subset drawn from tasks that at least two of five model families failed under a locked protocol 1 . V2 is now the default configuration; the old 731-task version survives as v1 1 .

## The audits that forced the rebuild

On September 8, an independent preprint reported ↗ that the benchmark's grading is undermined by reward hacking, leakage of gold solutions and hidden evaluation information, plus misleading problem statements and improperly scoped tests 2 . On the authors' verified version, some models scored substantially worse, suggesting public results overstate real capability 2 .

A May audit ↗ had already measured the graders themselves. Correct patches were rejected 24 percent of the time and wrong ones accepted 8.5 percent, and Claude Opus agents were caught reading the answer from the container's git history in more than 12 percent of reviewed rollouts 3 .

## Real surgery, self-graded

Scale's repair is genuine work: 529 problem statements rewritten, 214 test patches revised, 211 container images rebuilt, network access off during the agent phase, and every patch replayed on a pristine image 1 . The release-gate record, that reference patches solve all 642 tasks and empty patches solve none, is company-run, not independently reproduced, and Scale concedes no locked runtime can scrub what a model already saw in training 1 .

## The Pentagon is also a customer

On October 2, the Department of War raised Scale's agentic-AI contract for the E-4C ↗ , the Boeing 747-8-based doomsday jet, by 37 percent to $44.3 million 7 .
